standard.title: Create texts for familiar audiences
standard.description: create and edit short imaginative, informative and persuasive written and/or multimodal texts for familiar audiences, using text structure appropriate to purpose, simple and compound sentences, noun groups and verb groups, topic-specific vocabulary, simple punctuation and common 2-syllable words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students create and edit short written and multimodal texts using simple sentences, topic vocabulary and sentence boundary punctuation (AC9E1LY06). They have not yet created persuasive texts, used compound sentences, extended noun groups or verb groups, or edited for vocabulary precision.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can create and edit short imaginative, informative and persuasive written or multimodal texts for familiar audiences using appropriate structure, grammar, vocabulary and punctuation.

nodes.label: Selecting structure for purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select or plan a text structure appropriate to their purpose — imaginative, informative or persuasive — before writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the purpose of their text and name a text structure appropriate to that purpose before drafting.
nodes.typical_width: Plan texts across all three purposes — identifying structural features appropriate to each — and use planning tools (graphic organisers, sequence frames) to organise ideas before drafting.
wider: Compare two possible structures for the same purpose and decide which suits the intended audience better
Plan a multimodal text considering how written and visual elements each contribute to the structure

response_modes.reason: In Mode B, planning is the phase that governs all downstream creation. A student who begins writing without a clear structural plan produces incoherent texts. Making the planning reasoning explicit — purpose, audience, structure — before drafting prevents phase collapse.

nodes.hinge_reason: Without a structural plan established here, Nodes 2 and 3 lack a framework — students produce sentences and vocabulary that are grammatically capable but structurally incoherent, rendering the editing node unable to recover the text.
success_criteria: Student can name the purpose of their text before drafting.
Student selects a text structure appropriate to that purpose.

nodes.label: Constructing sentences with noun and verb groups
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use simple and compound sentences with extended noun groups and verb groups correctly and flexibly in their writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Write at least one sentence with an extended noun group and one compound sentence in a short piece of writing.
nodes.typical_width: Use simple and compound sentences flexibly across a short text, including extended noun groups and verb groups where appropriate to express ideas precisely.
wider: Review a draft by identifying places where noun groups could be extended to add precision or where compound sentences could be used to show relationships between ideas
Compare a draft with simple sentences only to a revised version with compound sentences and noun groups, discussing the improvement

response_modes.reason: Correct and flexible use of compound sentences and extended noun groups in produced text requires repeated practice with self-checking. Students who understand the concepts in isolation still produce errors in extended writing. Practice in writing and reviewing is the productive investment.

nodes.hinge_reason: Errors in compound sentence construction and noun group extension produced at this node carry into Node 3 — the editing node requires a draft with these features present to review; without them there is nothing to improve and the editing task collapses to surface punctuation only.
success_criteria: Student produces at least one compound sentence with two independent clauses correctly joined.
Student uses at least one extended noun group (noun + article + adjective) in their writing.

nodes.label: Editing for vocabulary and accuracy
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit their own writing by making deliberate vocabulary replacements and reviewing grammatical accuracy.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and change at least one vocabulary item (replacing everyday language with topic-specific vocabulary) during editing.
nodes.typical_width: Edit writing for vocabulary precision — replacing everyday nouns with topic-specific alternatives — and grammatical accuracy — reviewing pronoun use and sentence construction — using digital tools where appropriate.
wider: Use a revision checklist to guide editing across vocabulary, grammar and punctuation simultaneously
Compare a first draft and an edited version, annotating what was changed and explaining why each change improves the text

response_modes.reason: Editing requires students to coordinate structural awareness, vocabulary knowledge and grammatical knowledge simultaneously. Holding all three dimensions active while reviewing a produced text is the integration demand of this phase.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Annotation of changes — explaining why each edit improves the text — is a genuinely rich metacognitive direction. Advancing students develop explicit revision language that deepens their understanding of writing craft within Year 2.
success_criteria: Student makes at least one vocabulary change during editing and can explain why the change improves the text.
Student reviews for at least one grammatical feature (pronoun use or sentence construction) during editing.
